source_quote: In line with the University's mission, the General Education program aims to improve
answer: The General Education program aims to improve students' awareness and intellectual capacity to address complex world issues and to consider them thoughtfully in personal and professional decisions.

source_quote: Critical thinking in evaluating scholarly sources and arguments;
answer: General Education outcomes: critical thinking in evaluating sources and arguments; information literacy and modern computing skills; ethical decision-making; and commitment to continuous improvement and lifelong learning.

source_quote: Every RHU student must take 30–33 credit hours of general education courses,
answer: Every RHU student takes 30-33 general education credits across six domains: 21 mandatory credits from domains 1, 4, 5 and 6, and 9-12 elective credits from domains 2 and 3.
review_note: p.90 states 30-33 gen-ed credits, while p.28 (S005) states all programs include 30 gen-ed credits.

source_quote: 1 Communication Competency* 8
answer: Gen-ed domains and credits: 1 Communication Competency 8 (ENGL 210, ENGL 217, ARAB 212); 2 Humanities/Fine Arts 3-6 (approved list); 3 Social Sciences/Culture 6 (approved list); 4 Natural Sciences and Technology 6; 5 Quantitative Reasoning 3; 6 Community and Sustainability 4 (domains 4-6 per major requirement).

source_quote: * Refer to the introductory section of the college of interest for a description of courses
answer: Courses for gen-ed domains 4 (Natural Sciences and Technology), 5 (Quantitative Reasoning) and 6 (Community and Sustainability) depend on the major and are described in the introductory section of each college.

source_quote: This course helps students develop their ability to communicate effectively in standard
answer: ARAB 212 Arabic Language & Communication, 2(2,0): effective communication in standard Arabic for the workplace, including writing and orally presenting workplace documents in Arabic.

source_quote: ARAB 212 Arabic Language & Communication 2(2,0)
answer: ARAB 212 Arabic Language & Communication is 2 credits: 2(2,0), i.e., 2 lecture hours and no lab.

source_quote: This course reviews the fundamentals of good academic writing in English, teaches
answer: ENGL 210 English Composition and Rhetoric, 3(3,0): academic writing fundamentals, essay writing and research skills in persuasion and argumentation, research papers, and oral presentations.

source_quote: Prerequisite: ENGL 101 or TOEFL 550+ (paper) or
answer: The prerequisite for ENGL 210 is ENGL 101 or a TOEFL score of 550+ (paper) or 80+ (computer).

source_quote: This course is designed to help students develop effective professional communication
answer: ENGL 217 Professional English Communication, 3(3,0): professional oral and written communication, including emails, memos, letters, proposals, reports and employment correspondence, plus presentation skills.

source_quote: jobs. Prerequisite: ENGL 210.
answer: The prerequisite for ENGL 217 Professional English Communication is ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course introduces students to contemporary business principles of ethics and
answer: BADM 355 Business Ethics and Social Responsibility, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: ethical frameworks (utilitarianism, justice, rights, care, virtues) applied to conflicts of interest, sustainability and corporate governance.

source_quote: corporate governance are among the issues discussed in this course. Prerequisite:
answer: The prerequisite for BADM 355 Business Ethics and Social Responsibility is Junior Standing.

source_quote: This course explores the theoretical and practical ethical questions about
answer: CMNS 360 Ethics in Communication, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: ethical questions in interpersonal, workplace, community and mass/digital communication through theory and case studies. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course will explore the world of cinema, video shooting, and editing. Students
answer: CMNS 470 Videography in Media, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: cinema, video shooting and editing across pre-production, production and post-production, including trailers, interviews and an advertisement reel.

source_quote: This course teaches students rhetorical modes in short essays and journalism,
answer: CMNS 320 Creative Nonfiction, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: memoirs, reportage and reflective essays, concise and clear writing, and oral presentations. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course surveys key figures, movements, and texts in cultural studies from the birth
answer: CVLN 301 Civilization Studies I, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: key figures, movements and texts from the birth of civilization through the Middle Ages. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: the 14th through the 18th centuries. The concentration will be on the historical, political,
answer: CVLN 302 Civilization Studies II, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: key figures, movements and texts from the 14th through the 18th centuries. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: the 19th century to the present. The concentration will be on the historical, political,
answer: CVLN 303 Civilization Studies III, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: key figures, movements and texts from the 19th century to the present. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course introduces students to feminism by exploring its historical development,
answer: CVLN 320 Feminism Beyond Borders, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: history, waves and key issues of feminism and its intersection with race, class and culture.

source_quote: This course studies modern education principles and their application in elementary
answer: EDUC 201 Fundamentals of Education, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: modern education principles in elementary and secondary schools, teaching techniques, and views of schooling.

source_quote: This course introduces Special Education, with a particular focus on current practices.
answer: EDUC 211 Fundamentals of Special Education, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: current practices, common learning disabilities, intervention programs and the history of special education.

source_quote: examining major philosophical writings in historical context. Prerequisite: EDUC 210.
answer: EDUC 312 Educational Philosophy, 3(3,0), surveys the development of educational thought through major philosophical writings; its prerequisite is EDUC 210.

source_quote: This course draws on the theoretical and practical aspects of the study of literature for
answer: EDUC 360 Children's Literature, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: theory and practice of children's literature and its place in the elementary curriculum.

source_quote: This course explores concepts in art, music, drama, and movement for young children.
answer: EDUC 365 Art Education, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: art, music, drama and movement activities that develop young children's motor, social-emotional and cognitive skills and creativity.

source_quote: This course introduces first-year students to poets with intrinsic literary merits. In
answer: ENGL 214 Introduction to English Poetry, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: poets of literary merit, developing critical analysis and oral and written criticism. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course introduces literature through fiction, poetry, and drama. It introduces
answer: ENGL 220 Introduction to Literature, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: fiction, poetry and drama from British, American and world literature, close reading and interpretation. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This survey course examines current theoretical and applied areas of linguistics,
answer: ENGL 222 Introduction to Language, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: theoretical and applied linguistics, language structure, acquisition, variation, evolution and teaching. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: In this course, you will explore what drama is, its basic elements, and the evolution of
answer: ENGL 223 Introduction to Drama, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: what drama is, its elements and the evolution of dramatic structure through representative plays.

source_quote: Students study Shakespeare's representative comedies, histories, and tragedies in this
answer: ENGL 230 Shakespeare's Plays, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: Shakespeare's comedies, histories and tragedies in the context of early modern England. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course introduces students to the process and practice of imaginative writing.
answer: ENGL 235 Creative Writing, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: imaginative writing techniques in fiction, creative non-fiction and poetry. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course explores the works of major literary figures and authors representing
answer: ENGL 252 Introduction to American Literature, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: major American authors and literary schools from the sixteenth century to modern times in historical context. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: The course surveys selected works in English or in translation from non-Anglo-
answer: ENGL 300 Introduction to World Literature, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: non-Anglo-American works (African, Asian, European, Latin American, Middle Eastern) in historical and cultural context. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course will survey theories of language acquisition. It will address human language
answer: ENGL 330 Language Acquisition, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: theories of first- and second-language acquisition, language processing and motivational and contextual factors. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course explores the major forms of artistic expression from the ancient world to
answer: FADR 215 History of Art, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: artistic expression from the ancient world to the present, including Renaissance periods and 19th-20th century modern art.

source_quote: This course teaches students the basics of black-and-white digital photography. It is a
answer: GRDS 230 Photography I, 3(2,2), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: black-and-white digital photography with hands-on practice, framing, camera parts, and film printing and development.

source_quote: This broad survey course provides a narrative of British history from 1066, including
answer: HIST 210 History of England, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: British history from 1066, including political, social and cultural developments. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This is an elective course whose primary objectives are to familiarize students with the
answer: HIST 350 History of the Arabs in the Classical Period, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: early Arab conquests, early Muslim civil strife, and the Umayyad caliphate and Abbasid Empire.

source_quote: contemporary issues and to enhance their understanding from historical and cultural
answer: HIST 360 Contemporary History, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: contemporary issues from historical and cultural perspectives. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course examines the ties between Europe and the Middle East in the 19th and
answer: HIST 365 History of Europe in the Middle East, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: Europe-Middle East ties in the 19th and 20th centuries and Middle Eastern reactions to European intervention. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This elective course aims to familiarize students with key events that shaped the
answer: HIST 370 The Economic and Social History of the Middle East, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: key events shaping social and economic development in the Middle East. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: across ages and development are thoroughly explored through readings, research,
answer: HIST 480 Special Topics in History, 3(3,0), explores selected historical issues through readings, research, discussion and guest lectures; its prerequisite is consent of the instructor.

source_quote: This introductory music appreciation course is intended for students who wish to
answer: MUSC 201 Introduction to Music, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: basics of music theory and history, listening and analysis across classical, romantic, flamenco, blues and jazz. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: Music is considered one of the essential humanities courses at most Universities
answer: MUSC 301 Introduction to the World of Western and Arabic Music: Theory and Practice, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: history of Western and Arabic music, listening, terminology, tuning, the elements of music, scales, reading sheet music, chords, and guitar in Arabic music.

source_quote: This is a study of some major topics in philosophy. The course emphasizes theory of
answer: PHIL 301 Major Trends in Philosophy, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: theory of knowledge, theory of mind, determinism and free will, and ethics, using readings and films. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: The course introduces students to the major moral theories
answer: PHIL 303 Introduction to Ethics, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: major moral theories and thinkers on how to live and act rightly. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.

source_quote: This course introduces contemporary philosophical thinking on ethical issues in
answer: PHIL 307 Business Ethics, 3(3,0), a Humanities/Fine Arts gen-ed elective: philosophical thinking on ethical issues in business and techniques for resolving ethical dilemmas at work. Co-requisite: ENGL 210.
